Use dt=0.001, T=0.3, and run 300 implicit Euler time steps.
Use alpha=0.05.
Use a tensor grid with Nx=60 intervals in x on [0,1], giving x_i=i*dx for i=0..60 with dx=1/60.
Use Ny=64 periodic points in y on [0,1), giving y_j=j*dy for j=0..63 with dy=1/64.
Use 2nd-order central differences in both x and y.
Apply Dirichlet boundary conditions u=0 at x=0 and x=1 for all t.
Apply periodic wrap-around in y, so u(x,-1,t)=u(x,Ny-1,t) and u(x,Ny,t)=u(x,0,t) for finite differences.
Use implicit Euler time integration, solving the linear system at each time step with the discretized operator I - dt*alpha*(Dxx + Dyy).
Initialize u at t=0 as u(x,y,0)=sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y).
Compute the numerical solution at T=0.3 on the 2D grid.
Compute the reference solution u_ref(x,y,T)=exp(-0.05*((pi)^2 + (2*pi)^2)*T)*sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y) on the same grid.
Save "solution_agent_heat_16.npz" containing arrays x (1D length 61), y (1D length 64), u (2D array with shape (len(y), len(x)) so u[j,i]=u(x_i,y_j,T)), and metadata scalars T=0.3, dx=1/60, dy=1/64, dt=0.001.
Save a heatmap or contour plot of u(x,y,T) as "solution_agent_heat_16.png".
Print min(u), max(u), and the discrete L2 norm sqrt(sum(u^2)*dx*dy) at T.
Print the max absolute error and the discrete L2 error sqrt(sum((u-u_ref)^2)*dx*dy) against the reference solution.
